title: POC scoping - Data handling for POC (PII, logging, retention)
topics: deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
summary: Initial scoping call to align on success criteria and POC data handling constraints. Customer requires no PHI/PII persisted in logs, redaction at ingress, and short retention for prompts. Discussed workload sizing for 10k requests/day, benchmark plan (latency, cost), and timeline for 4-week POC with security review and pilot contract.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-02 15:00 UTC, Duration 55m. Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Redwood CSM); Dr. Priya Patel, Maya Johnson, Carlos Ruiz, Ethan Moore (NovaMed).

00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the account. Samir is our solutions eng, Lina will help with the POC ops. Priya, do you want to kick off with goals?
00:18 Dr. Priya Patel: Sure, thanks Alex. high level — we want to evaluate LLM-assisted triage for inbound patient messages. key constraints: must not persist PHI, we need audit logs for requests, short retention on prompts, and encryption at rest. timeline is tight — we want a 4-week POC followed by a decision.
00:35 Samir Gupta: Great, super clear. quick clarifying Q: when you say PHI not persisted, do you mean no raw prompts stored anywhere, logs redacted, and no full transcript retention?
00:48 Maya Johnson: Exactly. we can strip names and identifiers on our side but we also need Redwood to not keep full prompts in long-term logs. retain maybe 7 days for debugging only, and then auto-delete.
01:02 Carlos Ruiz: And we need to validate key management — our KMS must be used for any encryption keys, SSO for access, and SOC2 evidence.
01:10 Samir Gupta: Understood. to walk through options: Hosted API (Redwood API) by default logs metadata and can be configured for retention; Dedicated gives you isolated capacity and more control over logs; Private deployment (VPC) is the strongest for data residency and avoiding any third-party storage. we can also implement redaction at the edge or server-side.
01:28 Pr. Patel: We prefer hosted if it can meet controls because we want quick time-to-value. but if retention and KMS are issues we may look at Dedicated. what's the typical retention and redaction capability today?
01:40 Alex Chen: Currently, we provide configurable retention windows — default is 90 days, but for POCs we can set to 7 or 14 days and enable automatic deletion. redaction can be applied at ingestion with rules; we also support prompt hashing and keeping only embeddings for auditing. note: the transcription infra sometimes keeps ephemeral cache for 24-48 hours for debugging.
02:05 Ethan Moore: when you say "prompt hashing" — does that mean we can store hashed prompt fingerprints rather than the prompt text? also, can we prevent the prompt from being used to further train models?
02:16 Samir Gupta: Yes on hashing — you get a SHA-like fingerprint, non reversible. and Redwood does not train on customer prompts by default for hosted enterprise customers; we have a contract clause and an option to opt-out and enforce no-training with a legal addendum.
02:30 Maya Johnson: Great. on workload sizing: our expected baseline is ~10k requests/day, peak 600 RPS during a couple of hours. latency target is <300ms 95p for the triage flow. cost per inference needs to be reasonable — we'll use Redwood Optimize recommendations.
02:47 Samir Gupta: That's helpful. for 10k/day and those latency SLOs we'd recommend a small dedicated instance or a hosted plan with burst capacity. we can run a benchmark using your sample traffic — ideally you provide a 1% sample of production prompts with redacted PHI and we run both hosted and dedicated runs to compare latency/cost.
03:05 Dr. Patel: On benchmarks — what metrics will Redwood measure?
03:09 Samir Gupta: we'll measure token-level latency, end-to-end latency including network, 95/99 p99 latencies, throughput QPS, and unit cost (per 1k tokens) plus failure/error rates. also quality metrics — we can run a couple of golden prompts to validate correctness and regression.
03:24 Carlos Ruiz: For security review, we'll need SOC2 reports, penetration test summary, encryption key lifecycle docs, and a statement about log retention and deletion. can you share the security pack?
03:33 Lina Park: Absolutely. we have a security packet (link) with SOC2, ISO summaries, and details on KMS integrations. i'll share it right after the call.
03:40 Alex Chen: On prompt storage concerns: if you're worried about verbatim prompts being stored in logs, we can enable immediate redaction and replace with hashed ids. also we can disable transcript recording for certain endpoints. note: some 3rd-party monitoring (like tracing) may capture metadata; we can exclude prompt text from traces.
03:58 Ethan Moore: any gotchas around embeddings? we use embeddings for rerank and we want to store embeddings but not the raw prompt. is that straightforward?
04:07 Samir Gupta: Yes, storing embeddings only is a supported pattern. we recommend storing the embedding vector and the hashed prompt id. that lets you lookup without preserving text.
04:15 Dr. Patel: about retention windows — you mentioned 7 days. do you do immediate deletion on request for GDPR right to erasure?
04:23 Alex Chen: We support on-demand deletions via API and manual deletion requests via our support. for the POC we can automate a 7-day purge job and give you an API to trigger deletions.
04:33 Maya Johnson: Timeline: we need security review and internal legal signoff in week 1, dataset prep and redaction scripts week 2, benchmark runs in week 3, and final run + decision week 4. can Redwood support that cadence?
04:45 Lina Park: Yes, that's doable. we'll need your sample dataset by Dec 6 to hit that timeline. we'll run initial benchmarks as soon as we have the sample and the security pack is fine.
04:55 Carlos Ruiz: about SLA — if we do Dedicated, do we get uptime and latency SLOs?
05:02 Samir Gupta: Dedicated comes with capacity reservations and SLOs in the contract. Hosted has operating SLOs too but Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and isolation.
05:10 Dr. Patel: ok, success criteria — to confirm: 1) latency <300ms 95p on production-like traces, 2) no persisted PHI in logs, 3) audit logs accessible and immutable for 90 days (but prompt text only 7-day retention), 4) cost projection within our target per-1k-inference budget, and 5) security signoff.
05:30 Alex Chen: sounds good. i'll recap in the notes. any final Qs?
05:36 Ethan Moore: one more — are there any transcription or autosave features in the SDK that might conflict with our retention policy? in early tests we saw an SDK-level cache that kept prompts locally for debugging.
05:48 Samir Gupta: Yes, the SDK has an optional local cache for dev mode — it's off by default in production. we'll provide config to disable any local caching and set in-memory only operations.
05:58 Dr. Patel: thanks, this is helpful.
06:00 Alex Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the security packet, POC runbook, and an initial benchmark plan.
06:05 Lina Park: i'll set up a calendar for weekly check-ins and send the POC template.
06:10 Alex Chen: next steps and action items noted. talk soon.

End of transcript.
